no Figma license. no agency. no plugins I had to pay for.

the biggest open-source library of animated React components. those smooth hover effects and text animations you see on high-end sites? copy, paste, done.

hits.text:
This is how you create the next Star Wars:

1 - Get your own IP to go viral
2 - Partner with an amazing platform like Dreamina
3 - Grow your audience and team over 6 months
4 - Pitch your feature script to studios, actors attached and total views to date
5 - Get a greenlight as a hybrid feature film

(I don't talk much about our feature film because, though we've had multiple offers, we're still writing the script and waiting to choose a major studio until the project is fully packaged.)

More updates on that early next year but you can still follow our playbook to repeat the same success. 

Our mission in life is to tell great stories but also to empower storytellers. 

So it's the greatest job to be able to make our original films and then give away ALL of our prompts and processes FOR FREE. 

I love hearing stories of creators that have followed us (and get more views on their original series, haha!) because we firmly believe that a rising tide raises all boats. 

Also I really want to emphasize that though it's more fun to follow a creator than a studio, I get far too much spotlight for content that is made by our entire team at @genreai_. 

Whatever I'm a part of is made 100x better by our 30+ team members and artists that we work with on a monthly basis. 

You see them in our credits, but it's important to highlight the value of working with teams to produce at this scale. 

We now make 3+ Nexus episodes PER MONTH (plus BTS content) and it wouldn't be possible without our incredible artists and my co-founder @tawnyholguin who keeps our sky-train on the tracks! :) 

Let me know if you want me to share more about how we organize our projects, staff our episode pods or other details that go beyond "prompts". 

There aren't many AI studios doing content at this level and I will continue to share our journey and tips to anyone who wants to go on a similar path. 

As always, thank you to all the fans and viewers for supporting our content. We make this for you and hope you continue to enjoy where this universe is headed. 

Our episodes to date have been in many ways a bit of a story R&D lab where we're experimenting with characters, locations and animals that may make for great recurring characters but now we will begin to dip into a more linear narrative arc with consistent faces and places. 

You've seen just the tip of the iceberg with this epic universe of Nexus and the best stories will be coming out soon! 

A big shoutout to Dreamina for trusting us with this partnership and we can't wait to share more soon!

▲ Nace AI just released Drex for Search, which brings its Drex decision models to document search, so AI agents get cited pages instead of top-k chunks.

The key idea is that search is a series of decisions. Drex first classifies the question as a quick lookup or a deeper agent search. It then narrows the workspace from folder to file, section and page, down to table and column inside a sheet. Only the kept pages reach the LLM, and the answer cites the file and page.

The numbers, per Nace: 92.05% on BrowseComp-Plus with GPT-5, at 12.61 search calls per question, 16.6x fewer than the only entry ahead. 77.5% R@1 on VisDocAgentBench, 10 points above Claude Opus 5. 94.7% on MADQA with Gemini 3.5 Flash. On OfficeQA Pro, all 9 agent setups Nace tested needed fewer turns, with Claude Code on Opus 5.5 going from 18.5 to 9.1 turns.

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode can call it through the nace-mcp server or the CLI. There are also Python and TypeScript SDKs and a REST API......

outsiders.name: ▲ Marktechpost AI
outsiders.text:
▲ Nace AI just released Drex for Search, which brings its Drex decision models to document search, so AI agents get cited pages instead of top-k chunks.

The key idea is that search is a series of decisions. Drex first classifies the question as a quick lookup or a deeper agent search. It then narrows the workspace from folder to file, section and page, down to table and column inside a sheet. Only the kept pages reach the LLM, and the answer cites the file and page.

The numbers, per Nace: 92.05% on BrowseComp-Plus with GPT-5, at 12.61 search calls per question, 16.6x fewer than the only entry ahead. 77.5% R@1 on VisDocAgentBench, 10 points above Claude Opus 5. 94.7% on MADQA with Gemini 3.5 Flash. On OfficeQA Pro, all 9 agent setups Nace tested needed fewer turns, with Claude Code on Opus 5.5 going from 18.5 to 9.1 turns.

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode can call it through the nace-mcp server or the CLI. There are also Python and TypeScript SDKs and a REST API......

Full analysis: https://t.co/qSuVHIFB5i

Product: https://t.co/BkzUhMwq3H

Console: https://t.co/N2Tr1YdCZo

Docs: https://t.co/vREIJzLYMo
